key_insight: Clocked 3D-NAND-style tiers store bits with no per-bit transistor or capacitor; an oxide channel gives near-zero dark current; imec's planar IGZO CCD (>1e10 cycles, >200 s) supports the physics.
killer_doubt: Snippet CTE is only >98%. A 64-bit 4-phase vertical string needs per-transfer CTE >=0.9999 (256 transfers keep 97%). Serial 0.1-1 us access confines it to a buffer/capacity tier.
decisive_experiment: Build a 4-8-tier vertical IGZO CCD string (gate stack, hole etch, ALD IGZO) at a university fab. Measure per-transfer CTE vs clock rate and 85 C dark generation against imec planar data. About $400k.
prior_art: imec IGZO 3D CCD buffer memory: planar 142-bit, CTE>98%, >200 s, >1e10 cycles (via search snippet); 1970s CCD memories; overturns N-08 'open territory'.

key_insight: Separates must-persist state from bulk DRAM so idle banks can power off. The useful part is the OS policy, not a legacy-node die.
killer_doubt: A 180 nm SRAM cell is ~4.6 um2, so 32 MB (256 Mb) needs ~1,200 mm2 of array. Phones keep 8-16 GB resident, and discarding it costs relaunch energy.
decisive_experiment: Do an Android/server trace study: idle self-refresh share against app-relaunch energy when DRAM contents are discarded, with a PASR plus on-SoC SLC prototype. Under $100k.
prior_art: LPDDR PASR and deep power-down modes; OS-assisted sub-array DRAM power-down research (e.g. GreenDIMM); 32+ MB always-on SoC system-level caches.

key_insight: AFE back-switching releases ~10-20 uC/cm2 at a fixed voltage, a latent-charge plateau worth ~2-3 V of linear ZrO2 charge. That could give ~5x hold time with no taller pillar.
killer_doubt: Each decay and rewrite is a full AFE transition: best endurance ~5e9 vs >=1e13 for hot rows. ~10 nm grains make a 20 nm capacitor's plateau a staircase.
decisive_experiment: On TiN/ZrO2/TiN MIM coupons (50 nm-10 um), bias at the back-switch plateau and drain through a calibrated fA-pA leak to measure the hold-time multiplier. Cycle 10 ns full transitions to 1e12 at 85 C. About $150k.
prior_art: NaMLab (Pesic et al.) biased-AFE ZrO2 memory and energy storage; SNU and others' MPB-HZO high-k DRAM capacitors; Phase B N-01 (same endurance blocker).

key_insight: Its value is as the OS/CXL interface that lets ECC-paid capacitors and approximate multi-level cells (N-62, N-66) deploy across vendors, not as a standalone gain.
killer_doubt: One BF16 exponent-bit flip scales a value up to 2^128. At 1% BER a 1 GB KV cache has ~8e7 flips; only low mantissa planes (~30-40% of bits) qualify.
decisive_experiment: Run LLM inference with bit-plane error injection at 1e-6 to 1e-2 BER to find the tolerable byte fraction, then prototype MAP_LOSSY on an FPGA refresh-control platform. Under $150k.
prior_art: Flikker (ASPLOS 2011) critical/non-critical refresh partitioning; EnerJ approximate types; approximate-DRAM literature; CXL memory tiering.

key_insight: A nonlinear (gated-diode) capacitance makes one broadcast plate clock a parametric charge pump. Stored 1s are restored in place, with no row refresh, tRFC stalls or refresh controller.
killer_doubt: Leakage spans ~1e3x across 1e9 cells, yet one pump amplitude must serve all. A 1 kHz, 1 fF, 1 V plate clock costs ~9 mW/GB, about refresh's ~6 mW/GB.
decisive_experiment: Build a 1 kb open-PDK (SKY130/IHP) array of gated-diode, diode and access cells with an on-chip plate clock. Map bistable margin against Vt spread, 85 C leakage and clock energy, with and without resonant clocking. About $80k.
prior_art: IBM gated-diode 2T1D gain cells (Luk, Dennard, mid-2000s); Goto parametron pumped bistable (1954); Phase B N-03 gated-diode strip. Broadcast self-refresh: none found.

key_insight: Multi-electrode deposition inside one etched hole is the right instinct (one etch, many bits), but coaxial shells spend radial room the hole doesn't have.
killer_doubt: 4 storage and 3+ plate shells with ~5 nm dielectrics need ~50-85 nm radial build per side. Holes are ~40 nm today, so area grows 6-20x for 4 cells.
decisive_experiment: Do a geometry/TCAD study of radial build-up, per-shell Cs and a staggered-recess flow. Cross-section a 3-shell ALD stack in a 150 nm hole coupon. Under $100k.
prior_art: Double-sided cylinder capacitors (all DRAM makers); multi-plate container-capacitor patents; Phase B N-43 coaxial 2T0C uses the coax better.

key_insight: Field-collapsing crested barriers give large write/hold current contrast with no transistor. It is worth it only as a selector with a real capacitor (N-85), not as the storage node.
killer_doubt: A 20 nm floating node is ~6 aF (~40 e-), under the ~82 e- kTC noise of a 35 fF line. 1e12 tunnelling writes break the charge-fluence rule (1e2-1e5 cycles).
decisive_experiment: Fabricate a 1 um2 TiN/AlN/TiN crested-barrier floating node read by an integrated FET. Measure the 3 V/1 V current ratio, 85 C retention and cycles to failure. Under $150k.
prior_art: Likharev crested barriers (APL 1998); imec/Govoreanu VARIOT barrier-engineered flash; nanocrystal floating-gate memories; Phase B N-85 crystalline crested-barrier 1S1C.

key_insight: Clever failure-mining: log-time threshold drift makes off-leakage fall as the bit ages, and each access resets it.
killer_doubt: OTS off-current at ~0.5 V, 20 nm is ~1e-11 to 1e-9 A vs ~8e-15 A needed for 64 ms on 5 fF. Drift buys a few-fold per decade, not 1e4-1e6.
decisive_experiment: Measure off-current vs time after firing on back-to-back GeSe-class OTS cells with 1-5 fF on-chip capacitors, at 25-85 C, plus cycling. Partner coupons. About $150k.
prior_art: OTS drift is well characterised in Intel/Micron 3D XPoint selector work. 1S1C selector-DRAM proposals: Phase B N-85, N-87. Drift-as-retention: none found.

key_insight: Open-PDK shuttles make parallel circuit-level cell experiments almost free. That is better used as a vehicle for testing other ideas' circuits (e.g. I-04691) than for leakage search.
killer_doubt: The DRAM access-device tail (<=13 fA) comes from buried-wordline GIDL and trap-assisted tunnelling at ~1e19 cm-3 junctions. 130-180 nm open-PDK FETs share none of that structure.
decisive_experiment: On one SKY130/IHP shuttle, measure 50 access-device variants with an FPGA tester, then check whether the rankings correlate with TCAD of a buried-wordline DRAM transistor. About $30k.
prior_art: Tiny Tapeout community shuttles; OpenRAM open eDRAM/SRAM generators; university eDRAM retention studies on mature nodes.

key_insight: Retention-profiled reuse turns retired DIMMs into supply during a 4x price spike. The trust layer (a measured tail) is the only new part.
killer_doubt: DDR4 cannot plug into DDR5 platforms, so reuse needs CXL expanders. DDR4 already has hPPR/sPPR row remap and 2x refresh, so the passport adds a few % salvage at most.
decisive_experiment: Test 1,000 retired DIMMs for retention tails at 45-85 C and 1x/2x refresh. Compute salvage fraction and $/GB against CXL expander cost. About $200k.
prior_art: Microsoft GreenSKU (ISCA 2024) reuses DDR4 via CXL; ITAD secondary DIMM market; REAPER/AVATAR retention profiling; DDR4 post-package repair.

key_insight: Per-tier oxide Schottky diodes plus plate-line selection replace 15 of 16 access transistors: a linear-capacitor DRAM analogue of 1T-nC FeRAM, built with the 3D-NAND recess flow, no EUV.
killer_doubt: 0.2-0.9 fF tiers read destructively through a one-way diode: ~15-60 mV. Reverse leakage must stay <2e-17 A at 85 C (barrier >=1.0 eV). 3x 1-beta needs >=48 tiers.
decisive_experiment: Make a planar BEOL test chip in a university fab: one access FET, 4 MIM capacitors, each steered by a Pt/IGZO Schottky. Measure 85 C retention, read signal, disturb over 1e9 plate pulses, diode endurance to 1e12. ~$300k.
prior_art: 1T-nC stacked FeRAM (plate-selected, shared node; Sogang 2026 thesis, stacked-FE patents) (via search snippet). Diode-steered linear-DRAM version: none found.

key_insight: Idle Gen-8.5+ display lines cost ~100x less per area-tier than DRAM fabs and already run oxide TFTs. It is a capital-light capacity tier if sub-micron patterning on glass exists.
killer_doubt: Display litho resolves ~1.5-3 um, not 0.3 um. At F=1.5 um, 20 tiers need ~39 cm2 of glass per GB and cost ~$2-4/GB, no cheaper than DDR5 to make.
decisive_experiment: Build a cost/density model plus a 2-tier IGZO 1T1C array on a G2-G4.5 R&D glass line, with an NIL or interference-litho trial at 0.3-0.5 um. Measure retention and bitline signal. About $500k.
prior_art: SEL CAAC-IGZO DOSRAM/NOSRAM; Sharp/JDI memory-in-pixel LCDs; PragmatIC flexible IGZO ICs; Phase B N-36 glass-carrier cell line. Multi-tier glass DRAM: none found.
